description: i006 (alloc-multiply-overflow, snapshot s02) complete. One credible finding: drivers/virt/fsl_hypervisor.c ioctl_memcpy (FSL_HV_IOCTL_MEMCPY) lines 218-237 — userspace-controlled u64 param.count (copy_from_user at line 165) is truncated into unsigned int num_pages = (param.count + lb_offset + PAGE_SIZE - 1) >> PAGE_SHIFT (line 218) with no clamp, then sized as plain 32-bit unsigned num_pages * sizeof(struct fh_sg_list) (=32 bytes each) + 31 to kmalloc (lines 236-237) with no kcalloc/array_size/check_mul_overflow, and the fill loop for (i = 1; i < num_pages; i++) (line 272) writes sg_list[i].source/.target/.size (lines 275-282) for every entry, so a wrapped product (e.g. num_pages >= 2^27, reachable from count ~2^41 due to the 64-to-32-bit truncation) under-allocates and the loop writes past the heap buffer — the seed's exact count*size-to-kmalloc-to-loop mechanism crossing an ioctl trust boundary. Reported with medium confidence (get_user_pages_fast pinning and root-owned /dev/fsl-hv mitigate; hypothesis verified by source reading and arithmetic only, no runtime reproducer on the read-only tree). Twelve further allocator-adjacent multiply/shift sites were triaged and classified (11 safe with concrete clamps/widths cited: nfsd4 opcnt<=16, v4l2 check_array_args clamps, vboxguest VMMDEV_HGCM_MAX_PARMS, bfad/bnad len<=UINT_MAX>>2, ematch nmatches __u16, pvrdma 128-page check, tas571x constant len, xt_hashlimit size_t vmalloc, x_tables jumpstack; 1 unresolved: qemu_fw_cfg device-controlled count with non-overflowing 64-bit product). Bounded negative evidence: remaining kernel-internal multiply sites (arch/, mm/, tools/) and subsystem sweeps of netfilter/media/fs/xen-virt used six high-signal regex families and were spot-checked, not exhaustively audited; peer-transport handlers deferred to i009.
